what_happened: In job engm, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The user gave two limits that the reading missed. First, CI's token is read-only (permissions: contents: read), so CI cannot write a checkpoint. CI reads the newest checkpoint and judges incrementally on push, or replays fully on schedule. Checkpoints are written only by local runs (athena check --attribution when it passes, and athena land after a landing record) and pushed with the records writer. Second, a producer's working copy is a one-commit snapshot with no athena/records, so it cannot time this repository. Timing must be measured on a synthetic repository (for example 200 landings), labelled measured-on-fixture, and real timing taken after landing. The event does not say what the first reading wrote.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and the local repo view. It has no step that asks, for each action or measurement the reading assigns, who performs it and where, what permissions that place has, and what data it can reach. The CI workflow's permissions and the producer's one-commit working copy are facts about the environment, and nothing in the reading stage lists them. Criteria therefore assume that CI can write and that the producer can time the real records history. The earlier CI-checkout case (nry5) has the same cause: the environment is not modelled. This case adds write permission and producer reachability to that gap.
prevention: Add an environment-capabilities step to the reading stage. A short checked-in table would give, for each execution site (CI job, producer working copy, local operator run), its write permissions and the refs and data it can see. The reading must name the executing site for every write, fetch, or measurement criterion and check it against the table. Where the site cannot do it, the reading must either move the action to a site that can or require a fixture-based substitute with a measured-on-fixture label. A reviewer check should reject a reading with a write or timing criterion that has no site named.
proposed_request: Add an execution-environment capabilities table to the repo (CI job: read-only token with contents: read, fetches only the triggering ref; producer working copy: one-commit snapshot with no athena/records; local operator run: can write and push through the records writer). Make the reading stage name the executing site for every criterion that writes, fetches, or measures, and check it against the table. Reject a reading in which CI writes a checkpoint, or in which a producer times the real records history. Acceptance: (1) a test shows a reading whose criterion has CI write a checkpoint is flagged; (2) a test shows a reading whose criterion has a producer time the real repository is flagged; (3) a reading that uses a synthetic fixture of about 200 landings, labelled measured-on-fixture, passes; (4) the checkpoint design itself is unchanged: CI reads the newest checkpoint and judges incrementally on push or replays fully on schedule, and checkpoints are written only by local athena check --attribution runs that pass and by athena land after a landing record.
